title: History Complete 1: Modern India 1757-1857, Reforms & Uprisings

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Portuguese in India:
1. Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese Viceroy, favoured a 'Blue Water Policy' of controlling the sea rather than building a land empire.
2. Alfonso de Albuquerque was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India.
3. Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Almeida (1505) was the first Portuguese governor/viceroy and wanted naval supremacy, so he did not seek territory; Albuquerque, his successor, took Goa from Bijapur in 1510 to give the Portuguese a permanent base. Statement 2 swaps the two men.
questions.s: Spectrum, Advent of Europeans in India
questions.h: Almeida = Afloat (sea power); Albuquerque = Acquired Goa

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The English obtained permission to set up a factory at Surat from Jahangir in 1613.
2. Bombay came to the English Crown as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza and was later leased to the Company.
3. The farman of 1717 granting the Company duty-free trade in Bengal on an annual payment of Rs 3,000 was issued by Farrukhsiyar.
4. The 1717 farman was obtained by Sir Thomas Roe after his embassy to the Mughal court.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Roe's embassy (1615-19) was to Jahangir and won trading concessions; the 1717 farman was won by the mission of John Surman, helped by the surgeon William Hamilton, from Farrukhsiyar. Bombay passed to Charles II in 1661 and he leased it to the Company in 1668.
questions.s: Spectrum, Advent of Europeans in India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about European powers in India:
1. The Battle of Bedara (1759) ended Dutch hopes of challenging the English in Bengal.
2. The Danish settlements of Tranquebar and Serampore were eventually sold to the British in 1845.
3. The first Dutch factory in India was established at Surat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Colonel Forde defeated the Dutch at Bedara in 1759, ending their Bengal ambitions, and Denmark sold its Indian holdings in 1845. The first Dutch factory was at Masulipatnam (1605), not Surat.
questions.s: Spectrum, Advent of Europeans in India

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT among the crops/plants brought to India by the Portuguese?
questions.e: Tobacco, potato, cashew, maize, chilli and pineapple came from the Americas through Portuguese traders; sugarcane is native to the Indian region and was cultivated long before Europeans arrived.
questions.s: Spectrum, Advent of Europeans in India

questions.q:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
1. Battle of Wandiwash
2. Battle of Plassey
3. Battle of Buxar
4. Battle of Bedara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Plassey (1757) gave the English Bengal; Bedara (1759) removed the Dutch; Wandiwash (1760) finished the French in the Carnatic; Buxar (1764) made the English the real masters of Bengal-Bihar-Awadh.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Allahabad (1765):
1. The Company received the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa from Shah Alam II.
2. Shuja-ud-daula, the Nawab of Awadh, had to pay a war indemnity of Rs 50 lakh to the Company.
3. Kora and Allahabad were returned to Shuja-ud-daula as a gesture of goodwill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: After Buxar, Clive made Shah Alam II a pensioner (Rs 26 lakh a year) and took Kora and Allahabad from Awadh to give him, while Awadh was left as a buffer state and charged Rs 50 lakh. Statement 3 reverses this.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Match List-I (Treaty) with List-II (Governor-General associated with it) and select the correct answer.
List-I
A. Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)
B. Treaty of Bassein (1802)
C. Treaty of Sugauli (1816)
D. Treaty of Yandabo (1826)
List-II
1. Lord Amherst
2. Lord Cornwallis
3. Lord Wellesley
4. Lord Hastings (Marquess of Hastings)
questions.e: Cornwallis ended the Third Mysore War, Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance was accepted by the Peshwa at Bassein, Hastings ended the Anglo-Nepal War at Sugauli and Amherst the First Burma War at Yandabo.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Treaty of Bassein (1802) is regarded as a major step towards British paramountcy over the Marathas.
Statement-II: By this treaty the Peshwa Baji Rao II accepted the Subsidiary Alliance and gave up the right to conduct independent foreign relations.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Once the Peshwa, the nominal head of the Maratha confederacy, accepted British troops, a Resident and loss of an independent foreign policy, the other chiefs saw it as a surrender of Maratha independence, which triggered the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Treaty of Seringapatam, Tipu Sultan had to cede about half of his territory.
2. Two of Tipu's sons were taken as hostages until the indemnity was paid.
3. The Third Anglo-Mysore War ended with the Treaty of Mangalore.
4. Tipu died defending Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) closed the Second Mysore War, in which Hyder Ali had died in 1782. The Third War, fought by Cornwallis, ended at Seringapatam in 1792, and Wellesley's war of 1799 killed Tipu.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power
questions.h: Mangalore = Second war; Seringapatam = Third war

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Anglo-Sikh relations:
1. Kashmir was transferred to Gulab Singh of Jammu under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) on payment of Rs 75 lakh.
2. Punjab was annexed immediately after the First Anglo-Sikh War under Governor-General Hardinge.
3. Punjab was annexed in 1849 by Dalhousie after the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: After the first war the Sikh state survived under British control (Treaty of Lahore, Bhairowal) with a Resident; only the revolt of Mulraj and the Second War led to annexation in 1849. Do not confuse the Treaty of Amritsar of 1846 with Ranjit Singh's of 1809.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760), which sealed the fate of French ambitions in India during the Third Carnatic War, was fought between Count de Lally and which British commander?
questions.e: Eyre Coote defeated Lally at Wandiwash and captured Pondicherry in 1761; the Treaty of Paris (1763) then returned French factories but without fortification rights. Clive was in Bengal, Munro won Buxar, Forde won Bedara.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Subsidiary Alliance:
1. Lord Wellesley was the originator of the system.
2. The Indian ruler had to maintain a British force at his own expense and accept a British Resident.
3. The ruler could not employ any European in his service without the Company's approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The idea of lending troops to Indian princes for payment was used earlier by Dupleix; Wellesley only systematised it into a standard treaty. Its terms included the Resident, a subsidiary force and restrictions on foreign relations and Europeans in service.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Satara annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse - 1848
2. Jhansi annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse - 1853
3. Nagpur annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse - 1856
4. Awadh annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse - 1856
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Nagpur lapsed in 1854, and Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the charge of misgovernance, not by lapse. Satara (1848) was the first state taken, and Jhansi followed in 1853 after Gangadhar Rao died without a natural heir.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Statement-I: The system of dual government in Bengal (1765-72) proved harmful for the people of Bengal.
Statement-II: The Company held the real power through the Diwani but the responsibility for administration lay with the Nawab, who had no power.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Under Clive the Company collected revenue (Diwani) through deputy diwans such as Muhammad Reza Khan, while the Nawab held the Nizamat without funds or force, so there was power without responsibility on one side and responsibility without power on the other. Warren Hastings ended it in 1772.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Policy : Associated Governor-General
1. Ring-fence policy : Warren Hastings
2. Policy of non-intervention : Sir John Shore
3. Subordinate isolation : Wellesley
4. Doctrine of Lapse : Dalhousie
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Subordinate isolation (respecting chiefs' internal affairs but isolating them from each other, with British paramountcy) is the policy of Lord Hastings (Moira), not Wellesley, whose policy was the Subsidiary Alliance.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Regulating Act of 1773?
o: Prohibition on private trade by Company servants
Creation of a Board of Control to supervise the Company's affairs
Establishment of a Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta
Designation of the Governor of Bengal as Governor-General of Bengal
questions.e: The Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act of 1784. The 1773 Act made Warren Hastings Governor-General with a four-member council, set up the Supreme Court (1774) and banned private trade and taking presents.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Pitt's India Act of 1784:
1. It separated the commercial and political functions of the East India Company.
2. It created a Board of Control to supervise the Company's political and military affairs.
3. It increased the strength of the Governor-General's Council to five members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court of Directors kept commercial matters while the Board of Control handled political affairs, creating a dual system of control. The Council of the Governor-General was reduced from four to three members.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:
1. It ended the Company's monopoly of trade with India in all commodities including tea.
2. It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's territories in India.
3. It earmarked an annual sum of not less than Rs 1 lakh for education.
4. It introduced open competition for recruitment to the civil service.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1813 Act ended the monopoly except in tea and the China trade, asserted Crown sovereignty, allowed missionaries and made the education grant. Open competition came only with the Charter Act of 1853.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
With reference to the Charter Act of 1833, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India.
2. Macaulay joined the Governor-General's Council as the first Law Member.
3. It declared that no Indian would be disqualified from Company office merely on grounds of religion, place of birth, descent or colour.
4. It introduced open competitive examination for the civil service.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act made Bentinck the first Governor-General of India, added a Law Member and opened offices to Indians in principle; the competitive examination had to wait for the Charter Act of 1853.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
With reference to the Charter Act of 1853, consider the following statements:
1. It added six legislative members and separated the legislative from the executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.
2. It introduced open competition for recruitment of the Company's civil servants.
3. It fixed a definite period of twenty years after which the Company's rule would end.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act renewed the Company's charter without a fixed time limit, only 'until Parliament otherwise provides', which signalled that Crown takeover was near. Statement 3 therefore fails.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order:
1. Charter Act 1833
2. Pitt's India Act 1784
3. Regulating Act 1773
4. Charter Act 1813
questions.e: The Regulating Act (1773) was the first parliamentary attempt to regulate the Company, followed by Pitt's Act (1784), then the Charter Acts of 1813 and 1833 which ended trade monopoly and then all commercial functions.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1858:
1. It abolished the East India Company and transferred the government of India to the Crown.
2. The Secretary of State for India was assisted by a Council of India whose fifteen members were all nominated by the Crown.
3. Lord Dalhousie became the first Viceroy of India.
4. It provided for the entry of Indians into the Viceroy's executive council.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only the first is right. The Council of India had 15 members, 8 named by the Crown and 7 elected by the Court of Directors; Canning, not Dalhousie, was the first Viceroy; Indians entered the executive council only with the Morley-Minto reforms (1909, S.P. Sinha in 1909).
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1 (Historical Background)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Governor-General) with List-II (Measure) and select the correct answer.
List-I
A. Cornwallis
B. Wellesley
C. Bentinck
D. Dalhousie
List-II
1. Subsidiary Alliance and Fort William College
2. Permanent Settlement of Bengal
3. Abolition of sati
4. Post Office Act of 1854 and the first railway line
questions.e: Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793), Wellesley the Subsidiary Alliance and Fort William College (1800), Bentinck banned sati in 1829, and Dalhousie opened the Bombay-Thane railway (1853) and uniform postage.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT done during the tenure of Lord William Bentinck (1828-35)?
o: Resolution making English the medium for higher education (1835)
Introduction of the Doctrine of Lapse
Declaration of sati as illegal by Regulation XVII of 1829
Suppression of thugs under William Sleeman
questions.e: Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation tool of Dalhousie in the 1840s-50s. Bentinck's tenure saw social measures and the education resolution following Macaulay's Minute.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Warren Hastings:
1. The Calcutta Madrasa was set up in 1781 during his time.
2. Fort William College was established by him to train civil servants.
3. The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded in 1784 by William Jones during his tenure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hastings patronised Orientalism: the Madrasa (1781) and Asiatic Society (1784). Fort William College was a creation of Wellesley in 1800 to train civil servants.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q:
Statement-I: Cornwallis is often called the 'Father of the Civil Services in India'.
Statement-II: He introduced a well-paid, graded covenanted service, banned private trade and acceptance of gifts by its members, but reserved the higher posts for Europeans.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: High salaries removed the temptation of corruption and private trade, creating a disciplined bureaucracy, which is why he got the title; Indians were excluded from the higher posts, which is the other side of his reform.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q:
Consider the following events in the tenure of Lord Dalhousie:
1. Annexation of Sindh
2. Annexation of Punjab
3. Opening of the first railway line from Bombay to Thane
Which of the statements given above are correct?
(Select the events that took place during his Governor-Generalship)
questions.e: Sindh was annexed in 1843 under Ellenborough after Napier's campaign. Dalhousie annexed Punjab (1849) and the first railway ran from Bombay to Thane on 16 April 1853.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q: The First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-42), in which a British army was destroyed during its retreat from Kabul, began under which Governor-General?
questions.e: Auckland sent the Army of the Indus to place Shah Shuja on the throne; the disaster of 1842 came at the end of his term, and Ellenborough, his successor, then withdrew and annexed Sindh in 1843.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power; Administrative changes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about land revenue settlements:
1. Under the Permanent Settlement the state's demand was fixed permanently.
2. The Ryotwari system, introduced in Madras by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read, recognised the cultivator as the owner paying revenue directly to the state.
3. The Mahalwari system was applied in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
4. Under the Permanent Settlement a zamindar who failed to pay by the fixed date could lose his estate through auction.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mahalwari, involving the village (mahal) or landlord group, covered the North-Western Provinces, parts of Punjab and central India; the Bengal system was the Permanent Settlement with the 'sunset law' auction rule.
questions.s: Spectrum, Economic and Administrative Policies of the Company
questions.h: Sunset law: pay before sunset or lose land

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Wood's Despatch of 1854:
1. It was issued while Lord Bentinck was Governor-General.
2. It led to the establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1857.
3. It recommended a system of grants-in-aid to private educational institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Wood's Despatch came under Dalhousie; Bentinck's term ended in 1835. It recommended departments of public instruction, three universities on the London model and grants-in-aid, which is why it is called the 'Magna Carta of English education in India'.
questions.s: Spectrum, Economic and Administrative Policies of the Company

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order of their occurrence:
1. Wood's Despatch
2. Sanskrit College at Benares
3. Macaulay's Minute on education
4. Calcutta Madrasa
questions.e: Calcutta Madrasa (1781, Hastings), Sanskrit College Benares (1791, Jonathan Duncan), Macaulay's Minute (1835) and Wood's Despatch (1854) show the shift from Oriental learning to English education.
questions.s: Spectrum, Economic and Administrative Policies of the Company

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Permanent Settlement did not allow the Company to share in the later rise in agricultural income of Bengal.
Statement-II: The land revenue demand was fixed in perpetuity at the 1793 level, whatever the later increase in cultivation and prices.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Because the demand was fixed forever while cultivation and prices rose, the extra gain went to the zamindars and their sub-tenants, and the Company later found revenue inelastic. That is the direct cause of the loss in Statement-I.
questions.s: Spectrum, Economic and Administrative Policies of the Company

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about civil services under the Company:
1. Wellesley set up Fort William College in 1800, but the Court of Directors disapproved of it and established the East India College at Haileybury in 1806.
2. The Macaulay Committee (1854) recommended open competition for civil service recruitment.
3. Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to enter the Indian Civil Service, in 1863.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The directors wanted to keep training in England, hence Haileybury; the Macaulay Committee followed the 1853 Charter Act, and Satyendranath Tagore, Rabindranath's brother, cleared the exam in 1863.
questions.s: Spectrum, Economic and Administrative Policies of the Company

questions.q:
Match List-I (Uprising/Rebellion) with List-II (Leader) and select the correct answer.
List-I
A. Santhal Hul
B. Kol uprising
C. Paika rebellion
D. Khond uprising
List-II
1. Bakshi Jagabandhu
2. Buddhu Bhagat
3. Chakra Bisoi
4. Sidhu and Kanhu
questions.e: Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhals of Rajmahal, Buddhu Bhagat the Kols of Chotanagpur, Bakshi Jagabandhu the Paikas of Khurda (1817) and Chakra Bisoi the Khonds of Odisha.
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Faraizi movement was led by Titu Mir.
2. Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi movement in East Bengal.
3. Dudu Miyan organised the Faraizi peasants against zamindars and indigo planters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Titu Mir was a distinct Wahabi-inspired leader of Barasat (24 Parganas). Shariatullah began the Faraizis; his son Dudu Miyan turned them into a peasant movement against zamindars and planters.
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q:
Arrange the following tribal/peasant uprisings in chronological order:
1. Santhal Hul
2. Kol uprising
3. Bhil uprising in Khandesh
4. Khond uprising
questions.e: Bhils (1817-19), Kols (1831-32), Khonds (1837 onwards) and the great Santhal Hul (1855-56).
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Uprising : Region
1. Pazhassi Raja's resistance : Wayanad (Malabar)
2. Paika rebellion of 1817 : Odisha
3. Ho uprising of 1820-22 : Garo Hills
4. Velu Thampi Dalawa's revolt of 1808-09 : Travancore
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Ho uprising took place in Singhbhum and Chotanagpur, not the Garo Hills.
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Santhal rebellion (1855-56):
1. It was directed against zamindars, moneylenders and Company officials.
2. It originated in the Chotanagpur plateau around Ranchi.
3. It led to the creation of the Santhal Parganas as a separate district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Santhals, settled in Damin-i-koh around the Rajmahal hills (Bhagalpur-Birbhum), rebelled over exploitation by dikus; the Government responded by creating Santhal Parganas. The Ranchi area was the setting of the Munda and Kol movements.
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q: The Rangpur Dhing of 1783 in Bengal was a revolt of peasants against the oppression of:
questions.e: Debi Singh was the revenue farmer of Rangpur and Dinajpur whose extortions provoked the peasants under Dirjinarain; the indigo planter conflicts came in the nineteenth century (Neel Vidroh 1859-60).
questions.s: Spectrum, Popular Movements and Uprisings (pre-1857)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Leader) with List-II (Centre of the revolt) and select the correct answer.
List-I
A. Nana Sahib
B. Begum Hazrat Mahal
C. Kunwar Singh
D. Khan Bahadur Khan
List-II
1. Bareilly
2. Lucknow
3. Jagdishpur (Bihar)
4. Kanpur
questions.e: Nana Sahib led Kanpur, Hazrat Mahal ruled Awadh at Lucknow in the name of her son Birjis Qadr, Kunwar Singh was the aged zamindar of Jagdishpur, and Khan Bahadur Khan held Bareilly.
questions.s: Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of 1857-58 in chronological order:
1. Fall of Delhi to the British
2. Outbreak of the revolt at Meerut
3. Death of Rani Lakshmibai
4. Mangal Pandey's act at Barrackpore
questions.e: Barrackpore (29 March 1857), Meerut (10 May), Delhi recaptured (September 1857) and the Rani died fighting near Gwalior in June 1858.
questions.s: Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Revolt of 1857:
1. The introduction of the Enfield rifle with greased cartridges was an immediate cause.
2. The General Service Enlistment Act of 1856 required new recruits to be ready for service overseas.
3. Sepoys of the Bombay and Madras armies joined the revolt in large numbers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: High-caste sepoys of the Bengal Army feared loss of caste by overseas service and the greased cartridges, but the Bombay and Madras armies remained largely loyal, as did Punjab troops.
questions.s: Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Revolt of 1857 could not become an all-India struggle.
Statement-II: The Nizam of Hyderabad, Sindhia of Gwalior and the Rana of Nepal, among others, helped the British.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Without the support of major rulers, the South, Punjab and Bengal, and with British control of the sea and communications, the revolt stayed limited to north and central India.
questions.s: Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857:
1. The Queen's Proclamation of 1858 promised to respect the rights of Indian princes and religious freedom.
2. The Peel Commission recommended that all Indian sepoys be replaced by European troops.
3. After the revolt, the Crown recognised the right of princes to adopt heirs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Crown ended annexation and Doctrine of Lapse, and later issued sanads of adoption (1862). The army was reorganised with a higher proportion of Europeans, and artillery was kept in European hands, but sepoys were not abolished.
questions.s: Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q: Who among the following described the Revolt of 1857 as 'neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence'?
questions.e: Savarkar called it the first war of independence and Disraeli a national rising; Majumdar disagreed on all three counts. S.N. Sen viewed it as a struggle for religion that turned into a war of independence.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence (1857 chapter); Spectrum, The Revolt of 1857

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a work or activity of Raja Rammohan Roy?
questions.e: Satyarth Prakash is Dayanand Saraswati's work. Rammohan wrote the Persian Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, ran the Bengali weekly Sambad Kaumudi and compiled the Precepts of Jesus.
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements

questions.q:
Match List-I (Organisation) with List-II (Founder/Leader) and select the correct answer.
List-I
A. Arya Samaj
B. Prarthana Samaj
C. Satya Shodhak Samaj
D. Ahmadiyya movement
List-II
1. Atmaram Pandurang
2. Jyotiba Phule
3. Dayanand Saraswati
4. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad
questions.e: Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay), Satya Shodhak Samaj (1873, Pune) and Ahmadiyya (1889, Qadian) each answer a different social base.
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Henry Derozio taught at the Hindu College and inspired the Young Bengal movement.
2. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned for widow remarriage, which resulted in the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856.
3. Vidyasagar founded the Hindu College in Calcutta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hindu College (1817) was set up by Calcutta's elite with David Hare and others; Derozio taught there, and Vidyasagar, as Sanskrit College principal, took up widow remarriage.
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order of their foundation:
1. Arya Samaj
2. Brahmo Samaj
3. Prarthana Samaj
4. Ramakrishna Mission
questions.e: Brahmo Samaj (1828), Prarthana Samaj (1867), Arya Samaj (1875) and the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.
2. The Deoband school was founded in 1866 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi and others.
3. The Ahmadiyya movement was founded by Syed Ahmad Khan.
4. The Theosophical Society was founded in India at Adyar by Annie Besant.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Ahmadiyya was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (1889). The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 by Blavatsky and Olcott, shifted to Adyar in 1882; Annie Besant joined later.
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements
